what: Parker-Hannifin makes motion and control components: hydraulic and pneumatic systems, valves, filters, seals and fluid connectors used in factory machinery, aircraft, construction equipment and air conditioning.
customers: Aerospace manufacturers and airlines, industrial machinery makers, off-highway equipment builders and HVAC firms.
money: hydraulics, filtration, seals and connectors for factories and mobile equipment
hydraulic, fuel and engine components for aircraft, plus aftermarket parts
moat: Components designed into machines and aircraft that stay in service for decades, generating replacement-part sales at high margins.
risks: Industrial demand follows the manufacturing cycle
Debt of about $15 billion remains from the Meggitt acquisition
Aerospace production rates depend on Boeing and Airbus delivery schedules
Returns on capital are diluted by the price paid for acquisitions
opportunities: Aerospace aftermarket parts carry much higher margins than original equipment and grow with flight hours
Its own operating system has steadily lifted margins across acquired businesses
Defence spending increases demand for its aerospace components
watch: Aerospace segment margins and organic industrial order growth.
